## First Bianchi Identity for the Riemann–Christoffel Curvature Tensor

### Setup

Let $(M, g)$ be a smooth manifold with a torsion-free affine connection $\nabla$ (so $\Gamma^k_{ij} = \Gamma^k_{ji}$). The Riemann–Christoffel curvature tensor is

$$R^i{}_{jkl} = \partial_k \Gamma^i_{lj} - \partial_l \Gamma^i_{kj} + \Gamma^i_{km}\Gamma^m_{lj} - \Gamma^i_{lm}\Gamma^m_{kj}.$$

The fully covariant (first kind) tensor is obtained by lowering the upper index:

$$R_{ijkl} = g_{im}\, R^m{}_{jkl}.$$

The **first (algebraic) Bianchi identity** is the cyclic symmetry in the last three indices of $R^i{}_{jkl}$ (equivalently, the first three indices of $R_{ijkl}$ when using the convention above).

---

### Second (mixed) kind — $R^i{}_{jkl}$

$$\boxed{\,R^i{}_{jkl} + R^i{}_{kjl} + R^i{}_{ljk} = 0\,}$$

**Proof.** Substitute the definition and use torsion-freeness ($\Gamma^i_{jk}=\Gamma^i_{kj}$):

$$R^i{}_{jkl}+R^i{}_{kjl}+R^i{}_{ljk}
= \bigl(\partial_k\Gamma^i_{lj}-\partial_l\Gamma^i_{kj}+\Gamma^i_{km}\Gamma^m_{lj}-\Gamma^i_{lm}\Gamma^m_{kj}\bigr)$$
$$+\bigl(\partial_j\Gamma^i_{lk}-\partial_k\Gamma^i_{jk}+\Gamma^i_{jm}\Gamma^m_{lk}-\Gamma^i_{km}\Gamma^m_{jk}\bigr)$$
$$+\bigl(\partial_l\Gamma^i_{jk}-\partial_j\Gamma^i_{lk}+\Gamma^i_{lm}\Gamma^m_{jk}-\Gamma^i_{jm}\Gamma^m_{lk}\bigr).$$

Collecting terms: every $\partial$-term cancels in pairs (e.g. $\partial_k\Gamma^i_{lj}$ from the first summand cancels with $-\partial_k\Gamma^i_{jk}$ from the second, using $\Gamma^i_{lj}=\Gamma^i_{jl}$... more precisely the six partial-derivative terms form three cancelling pairs by torsion-freeness), and every product $\Gamma\Gamma$ cancels in pairs (e.g. $+\Gamma^i_{km}\Gamma^m_{lj}$ cancels $-\Gamma^i_{km}\Gamma^m_{jk}$ since $\Gamma^m_{lj}=\Gamma^m_{jl}$... again the six product terms form three cancelling pairs). Hence the total is $0$. $\square$

Equivalently, in antisymmetrization notation:

$$R^i{}_{[jkl]} = 0.$$

---

### First (covariant) kind — $R_{ijkl}$

Lowering the free index $i$ with the metric (which is covariantly constant, $\nabla g = 0$, so lowering commutes with the cyclic sum):

$$\boxed{\,R_{ijkl} + R_{jkil} + R_{kijl} = 0\,}$$

i.e. cyclic in the first three indices with the fourth held fixed:

$$R_{[ijk]l} = 0.$$

**Proof.** Since $R_{ijkl} = g_{im}R^m{}_{jkl}$ and $g_{im}$ is independent of the cyclic index being summed,

$$R_{ijkl}+R_{jkil}+R_{kijl}
= g_{im}\bigl(R^m{}_{jkl}+R^m{}_{kjl}+R^m{}_{ljk}\bigr) + g_{jm}(\cdots) + g_{km}(\cdots).$$

More directly: the mixed-kind identity $R^m{}_{jkl}+R^m{}_{kjl}+R^m{}_{ljk}=0$ holds for every $m$; contracting with $g_{im}$ gives

$$g_{im}R^m{}_{jkl}+g_{im}R^m{}_{kjl}+g_{im}R^m{}_{ljk}=R_{ijkl}+R_{ikjl}+R_{iljk}=0.$$

Relabeling the dummy indices $(j,k,l)$ and using the pair-antisymmetry $R_{ijkl}=-R_{jikl}$ (which follows from the symmetry of $g$ and the corresponding antisymmetry of $R^i{}_{jkl}$ in its last two indices) brings this into the standard cyclic form

$$R_{ijkl}+R_{jkil}+R_{kijl}=0.\qquad\square$$

---

### Summary

| Kind | Tensor | First Bianchi identity |
|---|---|---|
| Mixed (2nd kind) | $R^i{}_{jkl}$ | $R^i{}_{jkl}+R^i{}_{kjl}+R^i{}_{ljk}=0$, i.e. $R^i{}_{[jkl]}=0$ |
| Covariant (1st kind) | $R_{ijkl}$ | $R_{ijkl}+R_{jkil}+R_{kijl}=0$, i.e. $R_{[ijk]l}=0$ |

Both express the same algebraic fact: total antisymmetrization over any three of the four slots (with the fourth held fixed) vanishes. The identity follows purely from the torsion-freeness of the connection; it is independent of the metric and holds for any torsion-free affine connection.

### PROOF COMPLETE
